title: The Prom of the band room
premise: Vesper Ashgrove has perfected the art of invisibility: raise the kids, ace the classes, never ask for anything. But when band teacher Mr. Okonkwo pairs Vesper with longtime nemesis Juniper Vale for a semester-long arrangement project tied to the regional Battle of the Bands, the two are forced into a fragile, grudging collaboration. As rehearsals deepen into something like friendship—and something more dangerous, honesty—Vesper's carefully hidden home life threatens to spill into the open, and Juniper must choose between family loyalty and the truth about why she really quit playing. The novel climaxes on prom night, when the band room becomes an impromptu stage: Vesper wins the audition that matters by playing an original piece written for the siblings, and loses the championship on purpose, discovering that being seen is worth more than being safe.
about_author: H. M. Vane is the pen name of a former high school music-room custodian who spent a decade listening to rehearsals through the walls before writing a word of fiction. Vane writes quiet, luminous stories about kids who hold families together and the rooms where they finally exhale.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet the Ashgrove household at 6 a.m.—toast rationed, backpacks packed, Vesper running the morning like a drill sergeant before catching the bus. At school, Vesper is a ghost with a 4.0. Emotional beat: the exhausting competence of a kid who's been an adult for years, and the fierce pride taken in staying unseen.

chapters.title: The Locker Rule
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Establish the rules of invisibility: never borrow, never explain, never let anyone past the front door. Mom's night shifts at the hospital blur into a running tally of missed dinners. A flyer for the Battle of the Bands goes up; Vesper looks away first. Emotional beat: quiet dread that the system could crack at any moment.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Seated Second Chair
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Introduce Juniper Vale: brilliant oboist, sharp-tongued, heir to a family of professional musicians she's stopped trying to please. She quit first chair on purpose. She and Vesper have traded icy glances since freshman year. Emotional beat: Juniper's boredom masking a wound she won't name.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mr. Okonkwo announces the semester project: pairs must compose and perform an original arrangement for the spring showcase, graded on 'risk.' He reads names: 'Ashgrove and Vale.' The class goes silent. Vesper and Juniper stare at each other like a verdict. Emotional beat: trapped outrage on both sides.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. First meeting in the empty band room: hostile negotiation, split the work, never meet outside school hours. Vesper can't explain why—Juniper assumes laziness. They discover they harmonize on paper before they can stand each other in person. Emotional beat: grudging respect arriving ahead of permission.

chapters.title: The Sounding Room
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper drags Vesper into the old practice rooms, dusty and soundproofed, and plays something unguarded for the first time in two years. Vesper hears what's under Juniper's armor. Emotional beat: music as the first honest language between them.

chapters.title: Cracks at Home
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Little brother Theo's school calls about missed homework; mom's shifts double; Vesper lies smoothly to a social worker's phone call and hates how easy it's become. The arrangement notebook gets hidden like contraband. Emotional beat: the cost of carrying a household alone.

chapters.title: The Vale Family Recital
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper's parents stage a showcase of Vale achievements; her absence from the program is a visible wound. Her mother announces Juniper will audition for the conservatory prep program—the very thing she quit over. Emotional beat: inheritance as pressure, legacy as a cage.

chapters.title: Detention Harmonies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both get detention after a hallway collision turns into a shouting match. Forced to share a room, they accidentally sketch the project's core melody on the back of a discipline slip. Emotional beat: the fight that becomes a first collaboration.

chapters.title: Almost Telling
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Juniper nearly discovers Vesper's home life—Theo shows up at rehearsal, calls Vesper 'Mama V.' Vesper deflects with a lie that lands wrong. First real rift. Emotional beat: the terror that being known means being reported, separated, undone.

chapters.title: Juniper Quits Everything
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. After a brutal fight with her mother, Juniper quits oboe, quits the project, quits the band room. She tells Vesper it's nothing personal; it's a lie. Emotional beat: self-destruction as the only rebellion she's been allowed.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With the showcase three weeks out, Vesper works alone and realizes the arrangement only works as a duet—so does the story they've been telling themselves about each other. Vesper goes to Juniper's house and sees the Vale trophy wall, and the locked case with Juniper's first, broken oboe. Emotional beat: understanding replacing judgment.

chapters.title: What Broke First
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper finally tells the truth: she froze at her conservatory audition at fifteen, her mother never let it go, and the 'quitting' was shame wearing defiance. Vesper, in exchange, admits everything—the siblings, the nights, the lies. Emotional beat: mutual confession as the story's turning point.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Duet
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They rewrite the arrangement around two damaged instruments and two damaged histories, rehearsing in the practice room after hours. The band starts to notice. Rumors start, too. Emotional beat: hope with witnesses—terrifying and exhilarating.

chapters.title: Rumors and Report Cards
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A teacher flags Vesper's home situation; a guidance counselor requests a meeting. Juniper offers her family's lawyer. Vesper, proud and panicked, refuses help and pushes Juniper away—repeating the old rule: never let anyone past the front door. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by pride.

chapters.title: Prom Is Cancelled
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Budget cuts cancel prom; the senior class is furious; Mr. Okonkwo quietly proposes the unthinkable—host the showcase on prom night in the band room, open to the whole school. The Battle of the Bands becomes the dance. Emotional beat: a community deciding to make its own celebration.

chapters.title: The Audition Letter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The regional youth orchestra's final audition—the scholarship that could change everything for the Ashgroves—lands on the same night as prom and the showcase. Vesper must choose in secret and tells no one, not even Juniper. Emotional beat: the old instinct to carry it alone, now a conscious choice with a price.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Goodbye
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Final rehearsals; the arrangement is finished and it's unmistakably about them—about inheritance, about who you play for. Juniper senses Vesper hiding something. Vesper writes a new piece for the siblings in the margins of the notebook. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened by the coming secret.

chapters.title: Prom Night, Band Room
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The band room, strung with borrowed lights, fills with the whole school. The showcase begins; the Ashgrove kids sit front row; Mom arrives in scrubs, having traded a shift. The performance of the arrangement is transcendent—and Vesper slips out mid-set. Emotional beat: the highest point of belonging, on the edge of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Audition
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper discovers the audition letter, races across town, and finds Vesper mid-audition—then does the unthinkable: walks in and asks to play the second part, uninvited. The judges, stunned, let the duet happen. Juniper faces her frozen-audition past and plays through it. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing truth over rules; the wound finally answered.

chapters.title: Champions of Nothing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They make it back for the final Battle results: they placed second—Vesper timed their exit to forfeit the top spot to the rival band who needed the scholarship tour more. No one minds. The band room dances the last song. Mom, Theo, the Vales, Okonkwo—all in one room. Emotional beat: losing the prize and winning the life.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, coda. Weeks later: the scholarship secured, the household steadier, the front door finally open—Juniper doing homework on the Ashgrove couch. Vesper auditions for first chair, openly, and takes it. The last image: the practice room, two chairs, both occupied. Emotional beat: identity chosen, inheritance rewritten, invisibility voluntarily ended.
